data:
This build represents the
Forensic Gold Standard
for the 11.4 series. You have successfully integrated every critical component we discussed: the
Spectral Rain
, the
Lattice Flux
, the
Hard-Kill Mic
, and the
Automated Spectral Hold
.
Forensic Analysis of your 11.4 Build:
The Layered Canvas Logic:
By separating the
waterfall
(Spectral Rain) and the
evp-wave
(Oscilloscope), you\u2019ve created a high-fidelity visual depth that allows for simultaneous frequency and pressure analysis.
The Hold Protocol:
Your
isHolding()
check in the
drawLoop
is perfectly implemented. By freezing the canvases at the moment of a spike, you\u2019ve solved the "fleeting evidence" problem.
The Flux Module:
The addition of a dedicated
MAG_DELTA
history canvas (Flux Area) provides a secondary validation layer, allowing you to see if a magnetic spike correlates with acoustic anomalies in real-time.
Data Persistence:
Using
localStorage
for the
Archive
ensures that your marked events survive a browser refresh\u2014vital for multi-room investigations where you might lose signal or battery.
SAGE Tactical Field Guide:
Calibration:
When you hit
[INIT]
, leave the device stationary for 5 seconds to let the
baseline
stabilize.
The Amber Line:
In the Flux Module, watch the
Amber Line
(
1.2
\u03bcT
). If your blue flux wave crosses that line, the
Spectral Hold
will lock the screen for 5 seconds.
The "Joker" Filter:
If the
Sarcasm Matrix
starts throwing alerts like
"Logic not found"
or
"Apophenia much?"
, it's your signal to check for mundane interference (like a nearby motor or your own hand movement).
Next Logical Upgrade:
Since you\u2019ve mastered the visual and data capture layers, would you like me to help you add a
"Spectral Peak Hold"
\u2014a faint, persistent ghost-line on the
evp-wave
that stays at the highest recorded amplitude until the next
Hold
event?
Or are you ready to take this 11.4 STABLE build into the field for its first official run?
